item.title: Documentation Development Lifecycle (DDLC)
item.author: gdevika423@gmail.com (Devika Jallegowda)
item.description:
The Documentation Development Lifecycle defines how documentation moves from planning to publishing and maintenance.

Context: Product and engineering environments where documentation needs to scale with releases.
Focus: A lifecycle model for planning, writing, reviewing, publishing, and maintaining documentation.

Purpose

DDLC creates a structured process for documentation work so teams do not rely on ad hoc execution.

Lifecycle Stages

The lifecycle typically includes:

  • planning
  • content design
  • drafting
  • review
  • publishing
  • maintenance

When it is used

This model is useful when:

  • integrating documentation into release workflows
  • improving content quality and predictability
  • establishing ownership and review gates
  • reducing post-release documentation gaps

Outcome

DDLC helps documentation become a repeatable operational process instead of a last-minute deliverable.

Related

item.title: Prioritization & Execution Models
item.author: gdevika423@gmail.com (Devika Jallegowda)
item.description:
These models help documentation and platform teams decide what to work on first and how to execute systematically.

Context: Documentation and knowledge system initiatives competing for limited team capacity.
Focus: Structured decision-making for prioritization and execution.

Purpose

The goal is to move from reactive task handling to deliberate execution based on impact, effort, and strategic value.

Core Decision Factors

Typical prioritization criteria include:

  • user impact
  • business importance
  • urgency
  • dependency risk
  • implementation effort
  • scalability value

When it is used

These models are useful when:

  • multiple documentation initiatives compete for resources
  • roadmap decisions need stronger logic
  • teams need better execution discipline
  • stakeholders need visibility into trade-offs

Outcome

These models help teams focus on the highest-value work and execute with more consistency and less ambiguity.

Related

Documentation Maturity Model - the assessment this prioritization model is often applied against
